#4545. Every Brand Selling Sports Cars in the U.S. in 2027

From Aston Martin to Toyota, this is every performance two-door car for sale in the United States.

Whether you love cars or merely tolerate them as basic transportation, we can all admit that sports cars are cool. The best sports cars stimulate the senses, whether it’s the sound of a powerful engine or the scent of expensive leather. Sports cars make our lives better, and you'll be doing the world a service by buying one.

That's why we've gathered all the new sports cars on sale for 2027. Only two-door vehicles engineered and marketed by their manufacturers strictly for performance (and fun) are included in this list. We have lists for sporty sedans and SUVs, but not here. If you want the pinnacle of excitement from the world's most renowned car brands, read on.

The grandest of all grand tourers come from Aston Martin. The DB12 and Vanquish aim for elegance with their clean, timeless designs, while the smaller Vantage is gorgeous all to itself. For a 1064-hp hypercar with polished road manners, consider a Valhalla.

Bentley's brutish approach to sports cars is the same in 2027 as it was in 1927. The Continental GT is a heavyweight that can handle, as evidenced by the latest Supersports model. The plug-in hybrid models offer greater comfort, with up to 771 hp.

Since the Z4 roadster departed, BMW is without a true two-seat sports car. What's left are two hard-core M cars with small back seats: the M2 coupe and the M4 coupe and convertible. If you dislike BMW's latest Neue Klasse designs, these cars are Alt Klasse in the best ways.

While the Camaro is on hiatus yet again, Chevy has four enticing Corvette variants ranging from supercar contender to million-dollar winner. They all undercut their European rivals on price, too. A new 6.7-liter V-8 is in for 2027, and it improves the performance of the lower-end Stingray and Grand Sport models considerably. America's sports car is at its absolute peak.

Although most mere mortals won’t ever be able to purchase one, the Ferrari hype is real. The company's expertise in electronic chassis control, plus the sheer brilliance of its six-, eight, and 12-cylinder engines, are the gold standards of the sports-car world. Ferrari deserves every love letter it gets.

Since 1964, there's been a Mustang for everyone, though in 2027, everyone who wants a V-8 Mustang better have at least $50K. Affordability aside, the Mustang matters. It's a classic sports car with the sound, fury, and the hardware to compete with the world's best—and that includes the $328,000 GTD.

We're not including Honda's heavy hitter, the Civic Type R, since it's a hatchback. For pure sports cars, the Prelude fills in with a pretty exterior, but it's effectively a Civic Hybrid coupe that starts at $44K.

As the party animal of any sports car gathering, Lamborghini likes to play loud and could care less who it wakes up at 3 am. The Temerario revs to 10,000 rpm and kicks up tremendous amounts of debris from the exposed rear tires. The Revuelto SV has 1050 horsepower with doors that open skyward, as they should.

Lotus has gone through many ups and downs over the years, but it gets one car right. The mid-engined Emira sports car is an analog machine with a dialed-in chassis, sultry styling, and the distinctive character you'd expect of a hand-built British car.

Maserati's beautiful sports cars with their rich, decadent interiors and twin-turbo V-6 engines are often overlooked by wealthy buyers who would rather buy yet another black 911. For those with great taste and total confidence, the GranTurismo, GranCabrio, and the MCPura offer a distinctive alternative to the norm.

The fundamentals of an excellent sports car start with an MX-5 Miata. It’s small and remarkably lightweight, which puts Mazda in a class of one for building a two-seat, rear-wheel drive, manual transmission roadster that costs under $40K. It can also be had with a power targa roof in the RF (Retractable Fastback) model.

McLaren is re-doing its logo, but fear not: the cars are the same technical masterpieces that feel like sports cars of old. Whether it's the plug-in hybrid Artura, the roomy GTS, or the race-ready 750S, a McLaren delivers raw excitement with expert control.

AMG’s high-performance models are known for being hot, fast, loud, and desirable. The widebody CLE53 coupe and convertible, the iconic SL roadster, and the slick GT Coupe are the Benzes we really want.

Maybach glitzes up and quiets down the AMG SL for a plusher convertible with the coveted Mercedes hood ornament. But rest assured, an SL680 in Maybach form is ready to rip when asked.

An oldie and very much a goodie, the Z is a sports car legend with an illustrious history. The current model features classic lines and a manual transmissions, and you’re unlikely to see another one like it in the neighborhood. Sign us up.

The daddy of all sports cars, Porsche is the first and last name for engineering perfection. Without a 718 Boxster or Cayman for 2027, it's the 911's job to keep the brand's heritage in full swing across its dozens of variants. It's fantastic almost to a fault, as so many people buy them that they start seem ordinary.

As the only gas-powered rear-wheel-drive car in Subaru's lineup, the BRZ is an elemental sports car that, like a Mazda MX-5 Miata, is a great teacher of driving skill. It's basic, relatively cheap, and always fun.

Toyota was the mastermind behind the partnership that bore the original Scion FR-S and Subaru BRZ. With the latest GR86, Toyota's essence of simplified, driver-focused engineering is on full display, especially now that the Supra has departed.

#4544. Lucid teases its cheaper sub-$50,000 Cosmos EV in new video and images

Lucid has released a new teaser video of what looks like the Cosmos, its upcoming sub-$50,000 midsize electric SUV and the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker.

The clip gives us the clearest look yet at the Cosmos’ lighting, front and rear, after months of camouflaged prototype sightings. But the car itself is still about a year away.

Lucid posted the 1 minute 34 second video on X yesterday. The caption talks about “elevating the experience of movement” and says Lucid can’t wait “to share this feeling with even more people.” It doesn’t name the vehicle, but “even more people” is about as subtle a hint at a cheaper model as you can get.

Two frames from the film show the vehicle at dusk. At the rear, “LUCID” is spelled out in red illuminated letters across the tailgate, flanked by thin red light strips, with a spoiler cutting across the base of the rear glass. Up front, a sculpted LED headlight with a row of vertical segments sweeps across a red body panel.

That rear end matches the Cosmos design Lucid registered with the EU Intellectual Property Office in May, which showed the same spelled-out “LUCID” tailgate and rear-glass spoiler. It also lines up with the thin red light strips on the camouflaged Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101 in California last month.

Lucid unveiled its plans for Cosmos and Earth at its first Investor Day in March. Both ride on the new midsize platform and start under $50,000, roughly half the price of the Gravity.

On paper, the Cosmos is impressive. Lucid claims about 300 miles of range from a 69 kWh pack, thanks to efficiency of up to 4.5 mi/kWh, which it says is 10% better than its closest competitor. It also claims 200 miles of range in 14 minutes of charging, and its new Atlas drive unit has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the Zeus unit in the Gravity.

The problem is timing. Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, CEO Silvio Napoli pushed the Cosmos to 2027, “most likely the second half.”

That puts it on the same schedule as Rivian’s $45,000 base R2, and well after the Tesla Model Y it was caught testing next to in Arizona back in May.

Lucid needs this car badly. It delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while building only 2,954 after cutting the second shift at its Arizona factory.

I want Lucid to succeed. Period. I love the Air Pure and would like to get one at some point, but the cost is out of my budget while the tech is more than I want or need.

But I think what impresses me more than anything with Lucid is that they are one of the few who actually speak efficiency. It seems that they actually care about being efficient where companies like GM and others just build vehicles with bigger batteries in order to get more range. So for that, I give Lucid much credit.

The company is building hype a year out. It has nothing else new to sell until the Cosmos arrives, and the company reports Q3 earnings on Monday. They need to remind everyone what they are working toward.

A midsize SUV doing 4.5 mi/kWh would be best in class by a wide margin, and Lucid’s efficiency claims have held up on the Air. If it really lands under $50,000 with 300 miles of range, it’s a very compelling alternative to the Model Y and the R2, which still have room to take over market shares from ICE vehicles.

But Lucid has already slipped this car once; it says its cash lasts “well into 2027,” and the Cosmos is due in the second half of 2027. That’s a tight overlap. I think the Cosmos will be a good car, but can Lucid fund it all the way to customers’ driveways?

#4543. The Yangwang Altior is a Mega-Luxury Electric Sedan from China Aimed Right at Rolls-Royce

BYD’s luxury arm has an answer to those in the super-luxury end of the market with this quad-motor EV. It even looks like a Rolls.

Last week, Yangwang broke a speed record. This week, the Chinese luxury car brand is doing something rather different: it’s revealing a Rolls-Royce-esque full-size luxury sedan called the Altior. And sure, plenty of the details are unique to this Yangwang, but it’s hard to look at this sedan and not see the famous Ghost in its proportions (it’s about two inches longer than one) and design language.

The chassis and powertrain under this car’s sheet metal is nothing like that of the Rolls it looks so much like, though. Instead of a V-12, the Altior is fitted with a quad-motor electric powertrain, with all four electric motors independent from one another. Total output isn’t available, but we suspect it will have to be somewhere in the 1000-horsepower range with that many electric motors.

Yangwang makes several neat claims as to the car’s abilities. For one, it’s apparently capable of performing a tank turn; we’re not sure how useful that will be in a luxury sedan, but the possibility exists. An active body control system reads the road ahead and adjusts the suspension to provide the most comfortable ride possible. Yangwang also claims the Altior has an “emergency flotation capability” that can “provide additional support if the vehicle accidentally enters water.” That sounds similar to Elon Musk’s claims about the Cybertruck being capable of briefly acting as a boat ... and in both cases, we wouldn’t recommend testing the claim.

Power comes from what Yangwang says is its second-generation “Blade Battery,” and the claim is 621 miles of range on China’s very optimistic CLTC cycle. Charging specs weren’t revealed, but the Blade Battery 2.0 with “Flash Charging” (which the Altior has) in the Yangwang U7 has an astounding peak charging rate of about 1500 kilowatts.

The Altior’s interior is undeniably gorgeous, though it trades much of the ornamentation of a Rolls for the tech-forward screens we’re accustomed to seeing in high-end Chinese EVs. Hetian jade is used for the air vents, while semi-aniline leather is found on the seats, and Yangwang uses Suzhou embroidery (the technique involves splitting silk threads) to create flowing cloud motifs. Real metal switches are found throughout. The floor mats are made of wool, and natural woods were selected for the trim.

A four-seat layout and so-called zero-gravity seats with massage ensure the rear occupants are mighty comfortable. The car has a 39-speaker Dynaudio sound system, while a 21.4-inch overhead screen drops down to provide entertainment for those in the back. Plus, there are two fridges, and the one in the rear even has a warming function. In case you needed further evidence of the inspiration Rolls had on this interior’s design, there are even bespoke umbrellas that are integrated in the doors. (That said, Yangwang says it got the idea from the “Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at China’s Temple of Heaven complex,” with no mention of Rolls to be found.)

This massive sedan sure won’t see roads in the U.S., but Yangwang intends to sell it in Europe in the future, where it can go toe-to-toe with the British-made luxury sedans it borrows so much from.

#4542. 2027 Tesla Cybertruck

See all results for new 2027 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 29405

The Cybertruck’s styling gets a lot of attention, but under the skin is a capable and useful workhorse on par with other electric pickups. All models come with all-wheel drive, and a height-adjustable air-spring suspension system gives you more ground clearance for off-road adventures. A 593-hp dual-motor setup is standard; the Cyberbeast trim gets an 834-hp tri-motor powertrain.

Inside, you will find Tesla’s signature minimalist interior design, with a large center touchscreen on the dash housing virtually all of the truck’s gauges and controls. A yoke-style steering wheel and variable-ratio electric power steering take some getting used to, but once you’re up and running, you will find the Cybertruck to be easily maneuverable.

Expert Tip: The Cybertruck’s stainless-steel body comes unpainted. Plus, it attracts fingerprints just like your home’s stainless steel kitchen appliances. If that sounds like it might get on your nerves, you may want to consider the cost of a vehicle wrap in your buying decision.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has announced that production of the Cybertruck will end mid-2027, so if you want one, you need to act quickly.

Compare the 2027 Tesla Cybertruck with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

The base rear-wheel drive single-motor model from last year has been discontinued, leaving the dual-motor all-wheel drive variant to serve as the Cybertruck lineup’s entry-level model. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has announced that production of the Cybertruck will end mid-2027, so if you want one you ought to act quickly.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The base and Premium trims feature the same 593-hp dual-motor powertrain. Those looking for mind-bending performance will want the Cyberbeast, which features a trio of motors making a combined 834 horses. The Premium and Cyberbeast trims have an adjustable air suspension that can raise or lower the EV on the fly to provide up to 16 inches of ground clearance; the base models make do with conventional coil-spring suspension with adaptive dampers.

All Cybertrucks boast impressive 35-degree approach and 28-degree departure angles, so the Tesla pickup should be a formidable off-road machine. On the road, the big Cybertruck feels more agile than expected. We drove a Cyberbeast and found its combination of rear-wheel steering and variable-ratio steer-by-wire tech made for easy maneuvering in urban environments.

In Comparison: The tri-motor Cyberbeast's 2.6-second 60-mph time makes it quicker than the quad-motor Rivian R1T, which needed 3.0 seconds to get to the same speed. Even more impressive, the Cyberbeast's 60-mph time matches that of the Chevy Corvette C8 Z06.

The Premium and Cyberbeast models have a maximum towing capacity of 11,000 pounds, while the base trim is rated to tug 7500 pounds. Payload varies by model and tire choice, but an all-terrain-shod Cybertruck Premium can haul the most, carrying 2500 pounds in its six-by-four-foot composite cargo bed.

The Tesla Cyberbeast's battery capacity is approximately 122.4 kWh. Tesla claims the base model can recoup 132 miles in 15 minutes when hooked up to a Supercharger. In the same timeframe, the Premium model can restore 137 miles while the Cyberbeast adds 135. In our testing, it took 50 minutes to charge the Cyberbeast's battery from 10 to 50 percent.

Since the Cybertruck is technically considered a heavy-duty pickup truck by the EPA's standards, Tesla isn't required to report fuel-economy figures to the government agency. We observed 55 MPGe in mixed driving with a Cyberbeast.

First Row: Those who thought the Tesla Model 3's interior was minimalistic will relive that reaction when they see the Cybertruck's spartan cabin. The base model boasts heated front seats and a single central touchscreen, while the other two have seat heating and ventilation, plus a second screen for rear-seat passengers.

Second Row: Headroom is surprisingly generous in the rear seat given the truck's dramatically sloped roofline, but riders over six feet tall may find it snug.

Cargo Capacity: In our testing, we found that the truck's front trunk (frunk) holds just one carry-on suitcase, but the interior will fit 22 with the rear seats folded. The Cybertruck's cargo bed offers 121 cubic feet of volume, and inside the bed is a hidden underfloor storage compartment that’s large enough to fit an additional suitcase.

Every Cybertruck has a big 18.5-inch touchscreen mounted in the center of the dashboard. In the Premium and Cyberbeast, there's also a 9.4-inch touchscreen on the back of the center console for rear-seat passengers. SiriusXM satellite radio is included, as is a Wi-Fi hotspot, but drivers hoping for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto will be disappointed, as those features do not appear in any Tesla model.

Every Cybertruck comes standard with Tesla's controversial Autopilot driving feature. The brand's Full Self-Driving (supervised) system is optional. Neither system yet enables fully autonomous driving, something Tesla has long promised. The company also provides other, more basic driver-assistance technology.

For information about the Cybertruck's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Tesla provides a comprehensive warranty on its current models; however, it doesn't include any complimentary maintenance.

#4541. Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices up to 10% after announcing it will kill production

Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.

The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.

Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:

The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.

This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August, when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.

Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.

For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.

The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.

Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.

The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla canceled it for Australia and New Zealand last month.

So, Tesla has now discontinued more models than it currently offers. Looks like the great leader isn’t particularly good at writing product specs. And the hype has been over for quite a while anyway. In Europe, owning a Tesla has actually become something of an image liability.

This is what a wind-down looks like. Tesla isn’t trying to sell more Cybertrucks anymore. It’s trying to make as much money as possible on the last ones, with the hope that announcing the end of production will encourage some people to secure their order.

Once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.

But it does say a lot about the last two years of Cybertruck pricing. Tesla went from a $59,990 “limited-time” offer in February to a $92,490 entry price in November. That’s a company that never figured out who the truck was for.

#4540. Police Say BMW M5 Street Racer Hid His Face and Plates, But Couldn't Hide His Identity Forever

Authorities identified an allegedly masked BMW driver and arrested him at a Brampton, Ontario home after a three-month investigation.

It's no big secret that some folks treat driving laws like they're optional. To avoid getting busted for such behavior, some obscure their plates; others try to mask their face. One kid who allegedly did both around Toronto, Ontario is now facing serious charges because police still managed to track him down over the course of three months—and took his BMW away, to top things off.

Police in the Ontario region of Peel say they started tracking the suspect in August. On the 30th of that month, officers say they saw the driver of a red BMW M5 participating in a street race at 1:06 in the morning. It's unclear if they gave chase, but either way, they didn't catch the driver that day. Around a month later, police say they saw the car again; on September 26, it popped up at two different street racing locations as a participant, and the driver allegedly ran a red light in view of police. While they didn't snag the driver on that occasion, it appears authorities leveraged traffic cameras to start making a case. The driver was allegedly wearing a ski mask for much of his antics, and reportedly drove without a license plate.

A red BMW M sedan isn't exactly subtle or super-common. So, after a few months of investigation, police obtained a warrant and arrested Tarman Toor, a 24-year-old living in Brampton, and charged him with three counts each of dangerous operation, disguise with intent, and racing a motor vehicle. It's unclear if he's still in jail as of this story’s publication, but police say he has a meeting with a judge on the schedule in the near future.

Peel Regional Police say they they've arrested 119 people for traffic violations this year, and charged 214 with stunt driving in their area alone. Each one of those comes with a 14-day impound of the car in question and a 30-day license suspension for the driver. If convicted, Toor could face worse: several years in jail over just one of these charges, much less all nine of them.

BMW's latest Neue Klasse EVs push the boundaries of range and charging speed. In short, they're some damn good electric cars. Now there's another reason to buy one: free charging.

BMW on Thursday said it's offering $500 in public charging credits for 2027 electric models. It applies to the i5, i7, and iX3, and is open to drivers who buy or lease. The benefits last for one year from the car's purchase date.

Here's how the $500 breaks down. BMW says $300 of it can be redeemed at more than 15 charging networks, including Ionna, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, and EVgo. The other $200 only applies to Ionna locations. (BMW is one of the automakers backing Ionna.)

To access the funds, drivers need to set up an account through the BMW app. Once they do that and handle payment through BMW ChargingNetwork, credits are automatically applied to eligible charging purchases.

BMW is also offering buyers of 2027 EVs one free year of Ionna membership, which gets drivers 25% discounts on sessions at the fast-growing charging player.

If $500 in free charging sounds nice and you're considering these vehicles, I have one note of caution after getting behind the wheel of all three.

The i5 is a solid all-around EV. It drives well, looks familiar, and offers over 300 miles of range in some trims. But the i7 and iX3 are miles ahead in terms of onboard technology and specs. The latter models use BMW's Neue Klasse architecture and feature an overhauled digital interface with a wonderful "Panoramic Vision" display below the windshield. The iX3 offers over 400 miles of range and 400 kilowatt charging. Expect similar capabilities to trickle throughout BMW's lineup and into the next iteration of the i5 too.

#4538. Kia’s PV7 electric van stretches over 17 feet and seats 9

Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.

The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.

A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.

Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.

It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.

The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.

That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.

Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.

It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.

A plena capacidad la nueva #PV7 consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero #Kia #KiaPV7 #MovementThatInspires pic.twitter.com/fzIvviYZuE

Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.

Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.

Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.

With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.

The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.

Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.

The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.

Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.

The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.

The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.

Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.

The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.

Nice vehicle but once again Kia/Hyundai short changes on battery capacity. A 138" (3500 mm) wheelbase means plenty of room for a 140-150kwh battery (BMW and Rivian do that with vastly less space). That would give it a proper EPA range of over 300 miles with passengers or cargo. Instead this will be in the low 200s unloaded and 170-190 IRL. Offer it as a $7k upgrade. smh

Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.

The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.

Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the PV5 Passenger 5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

#4537. 2027 Toyota RAV4

See all results for new 2027 Toyota RAV4 for sale near 14094

Not only is the RAV4 one of Toyota's bestselling models, it's also perennially one of the bestselling vehicles in the United States. There are good reasons for that. The RAV4 sports a spacious and practical interior, 10 trims to choose from, plenty of bang for the buck, and, most importantly, great fuel economy.

When the RAV4 was redesigned for the 2026 model year, it dropped its nonhybrid powertrain, leaving a gas-electric setup that makes 226 horsepower standard; with all-wheel drive, the output goes up to 236 ponies. There's also a plug-in hybrid variant offered with 324 horsepower and up to 52 miles of electric range.

Expert Tip: For the price of a loaded RAV4, you might find a base-level of the larger Grand Highlander is more suitable for family duty, given it comes with a third row of seats.

Compare the 2027 Toyota RAV4 with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

Toyota has made a few updates to certain versions of the RAV4 for 2027, including the off-road-oriented Woodland, which gets a lifted suspension that now provides 9.1 inches of ground clearance. The plug-in hybrid model also now has a NACS charging port, meaning you can juice up at Tesla Supercharger stations.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The RAV4 Hybrid is powered by a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine and two electric motors that combine for 226 horsepower; front-wheel drive is standard. If you opt for all-wheel drive, a third electric motor is added to drive the rear axle, and horsepower climbs to 236. RAV4 PHEV models get a lot more power—324 horsepower combined—and feature all-wheel drive standard.

The GR Sport trim is the sportiest offering, with a suspension tuned by Toyota Gazoo Racing, summer tires, and a reworked power steering system. When we drove the standard RAV4 Hybrid, we found its acceleration to be responsive and smooth, but didn't enjoy the noisy gasoline engine. The RAV4 Plug-In Hybrid is considerably quicker, and the GR Sport model is slightly more fun to drive thanks to its tighter body control and sharper steering.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: The Honda CR-V Hybrid we tested tied the standard RAV4 Limited with a 7.1-second 60-mph time. Both the Mazda CX-50 Hybrid and the Subaru Forester Hybrid were considerably slower, turning in 7.6-second and 8.6-second times, respectively.

While front-wheel drive RAV4s and the all-wheel-drive LE trim can tow only 1750 pounds, the other models all offer up to 3500 pounds of max towing capacity.

Plug-in hybrid models boast a claimed electric driving range of up to 52 miles per charge; in our 75-mph highway range test, we achieved a real-world range of 38 miles in the Woodland trim. Toyota says the battery can be charged from 10 percent to 80 percent in as little as 30 minutes on a DC fast charger. All PHEV models come with DC fast-charging, courtesy of a NACS port on the driver’s side.

The EPA rates the RAV4 Hybrid to deliver 47 mpg city, 40 mpg highway, and 43 mpg combined in its most efficient, front-wheel-drive configuration. All-wheel-drive models are rated as high as 46 mpg city, 39 mpg highway, and 42 mpg combined. The more rugged Woodland trim is the least efficient version, at 41 mpg city, 35 mpg highway, and 38 mpg combined.

In our 75-mph highway fuel economy test, the RAV4 Hybrid Limited AWD achieved 36 mpg. The RAV4 Plug-In Hybrid Woodland achieved 35 mpg in this test. We don't yet have EPA numbers for the RAV4 Plug-In Hybrid, but Toyota estimates the PHEV at 41 mpg combined for the SE and XSE, 38 mpg for the Woodland, and 37 mpg for the GR Sport. For more information about the RAV4's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: A blocky design theme inside the RAV4's cabin gives the dashboard a rugged look while also being straightforward for the driver. The center console provides several storage bins, and some models feature a low-profile toggle-type lever for the shifter, which saves space and makes it easier to access items stored in the bins or cupholders. Most models come with either cloth or faux-leather upholstery, but sporty-looking XSE and GR Sport models feature faux-suede seat coverings with red stitching.

Second Row: The RAV4's cabin has enough rear-seat spread-out room for adults to get comfortable.

Cargo Capacity: Cargo space is reasonable. We fit 10 carry-on suitcases in the cargo area behind the rear seats and 24 cases with the rear seats folded.

A 10.5-inch infotainment display is standard, but a larger 12.9-inch unit is available as an option on some models. The system can support a Bluetooth connection with up to two smartphones at a time and offers wireless connectivity for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

A 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster is also standard, but if you want the available head-up display, you will have to spring for the Limited or XSE trims. Base RAV4s come with a six-speaker stereo, but a nine-speaker JBL setup is optional.

Toyota offers a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance features on every RAV4 model, including desirable features such as lane-keeping assist and adaptive cruise control included as standard. Other items are offered as options, including a 360-degree exterior camera system.

For information about the RAV4's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

All RAV4s come with a comprehensive warranty that matches those provided by rivals Honda and Nissan. Far from the norm, Toyota's complimentary scheduled maintenance policy stretches for two years or 25,000 miles.

#4536. BYD Offices Raided in Legal Probe Over Land Rover Defender Similarities

The BYD Ti7 bears more than a passing resemblance to Land Rover’s current off-road champ, but is that enough to make a case in court?

American buyers may not be familiar with the BYD Ti 7, a Chinese-made three-row hybrid SUV with a boxy shape and an unusual square of painted surface floating above the beltline. They will, however, be familiar with the Land Rover Defender sold in the U.S., a three-row SUV with a boxy shape and an unusual square of painted surface floating above the beltline. And according to a report from British newspaper The Times, Land Rover may have noticed some similarities between the two SUVs.

Last August, according to The Times, a court-ordered raid of BYD’s Dutch offices occurred on behalf of Land Rover company JLR. This was, reportedly, to find documents surrounding how a Land Rover Defender was used in the Ti 7’s development—evidence that could be key in a potential legal case over similarities between the models.

The BYD Ti 7 starts at the equivalent of $27,000 below the MSRP of the most affordable three-row Defenders on the U.K market. It also gets a plug-in hybrid powertrain alongside its seven-seat layout, while Land Rover’s plug-in Defender is only available in England with six seats.

Notably, Land Rover has already been involved in one lawsuit over another automaker attempting to build a product that looks astonishingly similar to a Defender. That model, the Ineos Grenadier, was cleared for sale in 2020 despite looking, well, much like an original Defender.

In the case of the BYD Ti 7, the visual similarities with Land Rover’s larger Defenders are obvious. The question is how much the two SUVs actually have in common, and whether or not it is enough to build a winning legal argument. Top Gear reports that a Dutch court will decide whether a case will proceed later this week.

#4535. The BMW iX3 smashed its EPA range rating, driving well over 400 miles in a real-world test

BMW’s new iX3 outperformed the Volvo EX60 and Mercedes-Benz GLC EV, driving well over 400 miles during a real-world range test.

In a recent nationally representative survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

The study found that 73% consider 75 miles of range, or less, enough to cover their daily driving. Meanwhile, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range to consider an EV.

Another 53% said they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in 10 minutes.

BMW’s new iX3 checks all the boxes. Based on BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive 800V system, the 2027 iX3 50 xDrive delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles (with 20″ summer tires).

With the 22″ summer tires, the iX3 50 xDrive has an EPA-estimated range of up to 392 miles. Still, plenty for at least a week of commuting.

It can also add 170-185 miles of range in 10 minutes with up to 400 kW DC fast charging. In everyday, real-world driving, it may drive even further than its official EPA numbers suggest.

During Edmunds‘ EV Range test, the 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive (with 22″ summer tires) drove 436 miles on a single charge, topping its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles.

The electric SUV was also more efficient than advertised. The iX3 achieved an energy consumption of 28.3 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles by roughly 11.6%.

BMW’s new iX3 is now the longest-range luxury electric SUV that Edmunds has tested, outperforming rivals including the 2027 Volvo EX60 (352 miles) and Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric (392 miles).

The Edmunds real-world range test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions.

It consists of 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

The 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive is available to order in Sport, M Sport, and M Sport Professional trims, priced from $61,500, $64,000, and $65,500, respectively.

Average speed of 40 mph in perfect weather is an absolute best case scenario for EVs. I think cold weather 70 mph would be the worst case and it should be tested.

That said, I think BMW and Mercedes tend to underrate their cars published range (I think they publish worst case condition range). BMW iX and Mercedes have historically outperformed EPA ratings according to various articles and reddits posts.

But I think regardless of what we think of Edmunds tests, these are some crazy range figures and with roughly 100kwh usable battery capacity, you are still looking at close to 4 miles per kwh. As an example across the Ultium platform anything from Chevy or Cadillac barely breaches 300 miles. The big Escalade and pickup trucks have 225+ kwh battery so I am not counting them.

If the depreciation rate for luxury EVs holds up, in 2-3 years, they will be awesome value.

Powered by a 108.7 kWh battery, the new iX3 with 20″ Summer Tires delivers up to 434 miles of range on a single charge.

With a charging rate of up to 400 kW, the new BMW iX3 can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 21 minutes, or add about 185 miles in 10 minutes.

Inside, the electric SUV features the Neue Klasse interior design. The setup includes BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a full-length windshield display, and a 17.9″ central infotainment screen running the latest Operating System X. Buyers can also upgrade to the optional BMW 3D Head-Up Display.

#4534. Gas Prices Got You Down? This 261-MPG Volkswagen Solves That—For $140,000

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In 2013, VW launched one of the most fascinating experiments in fuel efficiency ever made. The Volkswagen XL1 took 12 years to develop and ended up costing a whopping $150,000 at the time. However, as an engineering exercise, it was brilliant. And since VW only made 250, it's even rarer than a Bugatti Veyron from the same era.

If you're looking for an extreme answer to high gas prices, today's your lucky day. There's currently an XL1 in the Netherlands up for auction on Catawiki. The 2016 model up for grabs has just over 1,000 miles on the odometer and is apparently in excellent condition inside and out.

The XL1 project was spearheaded by Ferdinand Piech, VW's top boss at the time. Not known to ever give up on his lofty, ambitious goals, Piech fought for 12 years, and through several iterations, to finally achieve his "one liter" car, something that could burn just one liter of fuel per every 100 km. VW pulled out all the stops to make it extraordinarily efficient; the result was something closer to a supercar than a Toyota Prius.

That teardrop-shaped body is made from carbon fiber, as is its chassis, saving weight. It debuted a full year before BMW's i3, an EV/PHEV which only had a carbon chassis but a plastic body. The car has butterfly doors and two seats that are offset to optimize the car's aerodynamic shape.

Power comes from an 800cc, two-cylinder, turbo-diesel engine behind the driver—this makes it mid-engine, like a supercar—plus a plug-in hybrid system centered around a 5.5 kilowatt-hour battery. The plug-in hybrid powertrain wasn't originally planned, and didn't come about until near the end of its development, so it needed a massive 50-pound removable charging box in the trunk so you could plug it in.

With a funky hybrid powertrain, a curb weight of just 1,852 pounds, and a drag coefficient of just 0.189, the XL1 was capable of an EU-tested 0.9 liters per 100 km, which equates to 261 mpg. It can also travel 31 miles on battery power alone, registering an insane efficiency of 6.2 miles per kWh, about double today's more conventional EVs. VW said at the time of the XL1's launch that it only needed about 8 horsepower to sustain a steady 62 mph.

The main downside is performance: It only makes 68 horsepower, so it takes almost 13 seconds to get to 60 mph.

This specific car up for auction is expected to fetch around $140,000, according to the auction house. So even with its incredible fuel economy and currently outrageous fuel prices, the XL1's financial breakeven point is still a long ways away. Plus, it runs on diesel, which has seen even steeper price spikes than regular gas. A used EV cuts you off from the gas station entirely, and is a better all-around choice of course.

But for someone who wants an amazing piece of automotive history, the XL1 could be worth the price. Plus, it'll sip on fuel like no other for many of your daily errands—and look cool doing it.

#4533. BMW is throwing in $500 in free public charging with its new 2027 iX3, i5, and i7 EVs

BMW introduced a new public charging package for those who buy or lease the new 2027 iX3, i5, or i7 electric vehicles.

BMW’s electric vehicle lineup will look much different in 2027. The German luxury automaker is shaking things up with the arrival of its Neue Klasse EVs, bringing significantly longer ranges, faster charging times, and advanced new tech and features.

To sweeten the deal, BMW launched a new public charging promotion on Thursday for eligible model-year 2027 electric vehicles, including the new iX3, i5, and i7.

The new BMW ChargingNetwork package provides $500 in total credits. $300 of which includes a BMW ChargingNetwork credit that can be used at one of 15 public charging providers, such as ChargePoint, EVgo, Shell Recharge, and IONNA. The other $200 is for IONNA locations only.

Which one to choose? The 2027 iX3 is BMW’s first Neue Klasse vehicle. Based on its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive, the iX3 delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles.

The 2027 i7 also incorporates elements and tech from BMW’s Neue Klasse platform, with up to 362 miles of range.

The i7’s interior also gets the BMW Panoramic Vision display, a 17.9″ infotainment screen, and a standard 14.6″ passenger screen. For the rear passengers, BMW’s flagship sedan includes a 31.3″ 8K theater screen that folds down from the ceiling.

In the first quarter of 2027, BMW will launch the new iX5 and i3. Both are based on the Neue Klasse platform.

#4532. 2027 Lotus Evija

See all results for new 2027 Lotus Evija for sale near 30303

The Lotus Evija is a marvel of modern engineering, and not just for its astonishing acceleration, its stunning looks, or its incredible 2012 horsepower rating. Its genius lies in its ability to package heavy electric-vehicle powertrain equipment inside without abandoning the lightweight nature that Lotus’s sports cars are known for.

A torque-vectoring all-wheel-drive system helps get that enormous power to the asphalt, resulting in what we estimate will be a 1.8-second 60 mph time. This hypercar’s cabin also positions all of its key controls around the driver and minimizes distractions by forgoing traditional infotainment and driver-assistance features altogether. Unfortunately, even the mega-rich can't drive one in America outside of a race track, as it's not legal for U.S. roads.

Expert Tip: The Evija competes in the upper echelons of the hypercar market, vying for the attention of billionaire buyers alongside rivals such as the Aston Martin Valhalla, the Ferrari F80, and the McLaren W1. Unlike those cars, though, the Evija is not street legal in the United States.

The Evija rolls into 2027 without any significant updates.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Evija's electric powertrain is comprised of four electric motors that generate a total output of 2012 horsepower and 1257 pound-feet of torque. That's almost double the horsepower provided by hypercars such as the Aston Martin Valkyrie. A single-speed automatic transmission governs it all, sending power to all four wheels. The car's relatively light curb weight is designed to optimize handling. The company claims the Evija weighs in at around 4200 pounds, making it supposedly the lightest EV hypercar to enter production.

The car's performance can be customized via five driving modes: Range, City, Tour, Sport, and Track. On our test drive of the Evija, we were gobsmacked by its awesome power and nimble demeanor. Unlike some performance EVs that have a rock-solid brake pedal feel, the Evija’s carbon-ceramic brakes provide astonishing stopping power and can be easily modulated. We also enjoyed its hydraulic power steering, which provided more feedback than almost every other high-powered EV currently available.

In Comparison: We estimate that the Evija will be capable of hitting 60 mph in just 1.8 seconds. That puts it in contention with our estimated 60-mph time for the equally exotic electric Rimac Nevera. One car that actually went that quickly is the 1250-hp hybrid Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X, which scorched its way to 60 mph in 1.8 seconds in our track testing.

Lotus claims that the Evija takes a mere 18 minutes to juice from 10 to 80 percent on a 350-kW charger. Lotus said it expects its hypercar to deliver a 195-mile driving range. When we drove a prototype Evija on track back in 2021, we emptied its fully charged battery in just 15 minutes. That figure might be improved for the production model, but full-tilt driving is sure to zap range significantly.

Since the Evija isn't street-legal, it's unlikely the EPA will estimate its fuel efficiency. We're sure exactly none of the über-rich car enthusiasts who will be able to buy one will care.

First Row: The Lotus Evija seats two passengers, and its cabin is accessed via a pair of dihedral doors. The Evija's electrically adjustable front seats feature a carbon-fiber shell and thick pads swathed in microfiber. The driver can manually adjust the tilt and length of the steering column, and there are two bespoke storage spaces placed close to the occupants' hip points.

Cargo Capacity: There is no trunk or frunk in the Evija, and storage opportunities are limited inside the cabin. This is not a car for road trips or grocery-getting.

All Evijas come with tech features such as Bluetooth connectivity and an infotainment system. In front of the steering wheel, there's a digital display that provides the driver with pertinent information like battery charge and remaining range. This is the car's only screen.

The Evija comes with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capability, and Lotus has installed an onboard modem that facilitates connection to the cloud. A smartphone app is available that allows drivers to monitor the Evija from any location, checking on things such as battery charge status and driving range.

The Evija offers no traditional driver-assistance features such as lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, or automated emergency braking.

Lotus doesn't offer a particularly impressive limited or powertrain warranty. The company also doesn't include any complimentary scheduled maintenance.

#4531. Tesla Is Killing The Cybertruck To Make Room For More Robotaxis

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The controversial Tesla Cybertruck electric pickup will be retired next year, CEO Elon Musk confirmed on X. The angular truck went on sale at the end of 2023 and instantly became a social statement—for better or worse.

Production of the Cybertruck will start winding down next summer at the company’s Texas Gigafactory, and the extra floor space will be used to build more Cybercabs.

The unpainted truck had a short burst in popularity at the beginning of its production run, but interest fizzled, and sales never reached the potential that Musk and Tesla had envisioned back in 2019, when the vehicle was first presented as a concept.

In this year’s third quarter, the Cybertruck amassed 4,323 sales, according to data from Cox Automotive. From January through September, sales totaled 11,586 units. Tesla doesn’t break out individual sales figures for the Cybertruck, but industry estimates put the vehicle’s overall deliveries at roughly 70,000.

That’s a far cry from the hundreds of thousands of sales recorded every quarter by the Model 3 and Model Y. It’s also another reminder that electric pickups haven’t quite taken off as their manufacturers had hoped, and Tesla is now taking the fall, just like Ford did with the F-150 Lightning, which went the way of the dodo last year after lackluster sales and ballooning costs.

There’s no denying that you either love or hate the Cybertruck, just like there’s no denying that Tesla dared to do things like no other car manufacturer before it. Sure, some might argue that the angular EV looks like an unpolished fridge, but it brought steer-by-wire and a 48-volt low-voltage architecture to the masses. Whether or not they’ll be adopted by other companies is another story, though.

At roughly the same time as Elon Musk’s announcement that Cybertruck production would wind down in the middle of 2027, Tesla stopped taking orders for the entry-level Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive version of the model, leaving just the Premium and Cyberbeast trims available to order on the automaker’s website.

Additionally, the price of the remaining models has been increased. The Premium AWD model now starts at $92,490, up from $89,990, while the top Cyberbeast now costs $102,490, up from $99,990. The most recent price bumps come after a similar move in August.

#4530. Ford May Have a Replacement for the Shelby GT350 Mustang in the Works

A report citing dealer documents claim a new naturally aspirated ‘Stang will pick up where the GT350 left off.

The sixth-generation Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 was an enthusiast’s favorite. It offered a track-ready middle ground between the standard V-8-powered GT and the supercharged Shelby GT500, with a 5.2-liter naturally aspirated “Voodoo” V-8 pumping out 526 horsepower and revving to 8250 rpm, and a 6-speed manual transmission. The GT350 left production in 2020; Ford has not replaced it with a like-for-like variant for in the current seventh-generation Mustang lineup. But that could change as soon as next year.

Ford Authority is reporting that Ford sent out dealer documents confirming a new high-performance Mustang. The new Mustang would not be called the Shelby GT350—Ford has not used Shelby branding for the S650-generation Mustang, and Shelby American is currently building its own GT350. But the new model would, it seems, fulfill that role in the lineup. (Road & Track reached out to Ford for comment on the potential new Mustang, but a spokesperson only noted the brand “can’t comment on speculation” about future vehicles.)

The report claims the new Mustang would slot between the current Mustang Dark Horse and the Dark Horse SC, and would feature either a 5.2-liter or 5.4-liter naturally aspirated V-8. A six-speed manual transmission would be available, if not the only option, and the new Mustang—unlike the Dark Horse SC—would only be available as a coupe. Per the report, it would arrive in late 2027 as a 2028 model-year vehicle and have a limited production run through the 2029 model year.

Firm performance specs were not detailed for the potential new Mustang, but Ford Authority expects the power output to be around 600 hp, slotting between the 500-hp Mustang Dark Horse and the 795-hp Mustang Dark Horse SC. No word yet on pricing, either; however, the current Mustang lineup has a large gap between the $72,760 Dark Horse Premium and the $108,085 Dark Horse SC where this vehicle would fit in nicely.

Ford has been looking at options to “expand on the Mustang family,” with reported ideas including non-traditional variants such as a four-door coupe-style sedan and even an off-road variant. Reviving the manual GT350 Mustang, at least in spirit, would counter those sacrilegious notions with some welcome red meat for enthusiasts.

#4527. BMW Sets 2 New Nürburgring Records With Help from Pirelli

A revised semi-slick tire helped the carmaker knock down the compact car and touring car lap records at the Nordschleife.

Pirelli’s P Zero Trofeo RS is one of its most extreme performance tires, one capable of helping performance cars extract the most out of their potential. And that’s especially true when the company works with automakers directly—as the Italian rubbermaker did with BMW, developed a bespoke version specifically for the BMW M range. The new semi-slick tire remains street legal, but doesn’t sacrifice at-the-limit grip. And it helped BMW set two new ‘Ring lap records with its BMW M2 with the M Performance Track Kit and BMW M3 CS Touring.

The BMW M2 with the M Performance Track Kit managed a lap time of 7:25.068minutes. This lowered the Nürburgring Nordschleife compact car record, previously held by the M2 CS, by 0.5 seconds. The long-roof BMW M3, however, made more significant history: BMW’s M3 CS Touring lapped the 12.9-mile racetrack in 7:29.49 minutes, setting a new record for the fastest touring car ever by shaving off more than five seconds. The previous touring car lap record of 7:35.06 was held by the standard BMW M3 Touring. A combination of increased horsepower, stronger brakes, and custom rubber—as well as BMW M Development engineer Jörg Weidinger behind the wheel—pushed the wagon to success.

“The bespoke development program is the result of close collaboration between Pirelli and BMW M’s R&D teams. Thanks to advanced virtual development techniques, the two teams were able to adapt the tire’s characteristics to the different requirements from the earliest stages of the project, in line with Pirelli’s Perfect Fit approach, which aims to create products tailored to each specific model or application,” the tire maker said in a statement.

Pirelli initially tested the tires alongside BMW at the Nürburgring Nordschleife, and the tires were also later tested at the Nardò test circuit in Italy. BMW and Pirelli have collaborated on over 30 bespoke tire projects across the P Zero family over the years, and like many others, a keen eye can tell which ones are made for Bimmers; the manufacturer-specific tires feature a BMW star marking, as a nod to the integrated development process.

The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

#4525. Over A Quarter Of BMW, Mini, And Rolls-Royce Models Sold In Q3 Had A Plug

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The BMW Group, which operates the BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce car brands, saw 20% of its global vehicle sales in the third quarter represented by all-electric models. Adding plug-in hybrids increases the electrified models’ share to 27.4%, the company said in its latest earnings report.

From the beginning of the year through September, EVs have accounted for 18.4% of the three automakers’ total sales worldwide, with PHEVs raising the figure to 26.1%.

Despite the promising numbers, the automotive group clearly has a regionalization problem on its hands. Europe is leading the way by a wide margin, with 34.7% of sales represented by EVs and 46.9% by all electrified models.

Meanwhile, over in the United States, just 4.7% of BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce models sold were EVs. That’s a huge difference, and it puts the U.S. at the bottom of the BMW Group’s list for electrification. By comparison, Chinese EV sales amounted to 6.5%, while the Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa regions totaled 18% EV sales.

The only thing that saves the day for the company’s electrified lineup in the U.S. is plug-in hybrids, which, together with EVs, had an 11.4% share in the third quarter. It’s also worth noting that the new iX3 and i3 models are just starting to trickle down to American dealers, and the U.S. also doesn’t get the electric iX2 and iX2 that Europeans have access to. The updated i7 is also on its way, but that has always been a low-volume car that never made a meaningful impact on the company’s sales reports.

What’s more, even though one in every five BMW Group models was all-electric in Q3, the company’s year-to-date numbers aren’t so promising. Globally, the group sold 314,552 EVs and 131,653 PHEVs from January through September, a 5.1% decrease compared to the same period last year. EVs saw a 2.7% drop, while PHEV sales declined 10.3%.

The only positive number in the company’s electrification Excel sheets has to do with how many EVs were sold in comparison to everything else in the portfolio. In the first three quarters of 2026, the share of EV sales within the BMW Group reached 18.4%, up from last year’s 18%.

Things should improve once the iX3 and i3 are widely available everywhere in the world, but they’re not guaranteed to be a success in the U.S., where policy whiplash has severely slowed the adoption of all-electric vehicles.

Expert Tip: If you want an electric Jeep and don’t need the Recon’s ground clearance and off-road capability, the Wagoneer S is a more luxurious option with more driving range.

A luxurious Overland trim joins the lineup for 2027. This more road-friendly variant is said to have a slightly longer 240-mile driving range estimate, and it wears a more upscale look due to body-colored fender flares and 20-inch alloy wheels. Elsewhere, a NACS charging port replaces last year’s CCS connector, so replenishing the battery at Tesla Superchargers is now possible.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Jeep Recon EV utilizes a pair of electric motors, with one drive unit mounted in the front and another in the rear. They produce a combined output of 670 horsepower—serious muscle that delivers impressive acceleration.

In addition to standard all-wheel drive, the Recon touts features that should make it a stout off-road performer as well: an electric locking differential, 9.1 inches of ground clearance, and a Select-Terrain traction management system with rock, sand, and snow drive modes. When we drove the Recon, we found it to be entertainingly quick on the road, with better ride quality and handling when compared to the gas-powered Wrangler. Off-road, its touchy throttle and sensitive brakes make it more difficult to pilot, but it’s plenty capable in the dirt.

In Comparison: A 3.5-second 60 mph dash is mighty quick for a mid-size SUV, especially one focused on off-road capabilities.

The Recon EV is capable of towing up to 3300 pounds when equipped with the Trailer Tow Group package. That's a bit less than the 3,500-pound rating for the Wagoneer S.

With its 100.5-kWh battery pack fully juiced, the EPA rates the Moab trim to deliver 222 miles of all-electric driving range. The Overland trim is estimated at 240 miles. In our real-world 75-mph highway test, the Moab achieved a disappointing result of just 160 miles.

The Recon employs a 400-volt electric architecture and is capable of charging from 20 to 80 percent in a claimed 28 minutes on a DC fast charger. Level 2 charging on a 240-volt circuit should take the battery from 5 to 80 percent in roughly 7 hours. Drivers with no other option other than plugging into a typical 110-volt household circuit best pack a book or three, as the estimated time for a 5-80 percent charge in that scenario is up to 52 hours.

The EPA hasn’t released fuel economy for the Overland yet, but the Moab is rated for 80 MPGe city, 62 MPGe highway, and 71 MPGe combined. MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV vehicle fuel efficiency. For more information about the Recon's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

Second Row: It's a pretty standard affair in the back, with 60/40 split bench seating in the second row. Heated outboard second-row seats are available as part of the optional Comfort Package.

Cargo Capacity: In addition to the 30 cubic feet of cargo space behind the Recon’s rear seats, it also features a small 3.0-cubic-foot frunk under the hood—a perk of being an EV.

The Recon's interior features a central 14.5-inch infotainment display and a 12.3-inch digital gauge display offering readouts for the driver.

The company's Uconnect 5 software interface allows users to access all sorts of features, including Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, SiriusXM satellite radio, integrated navigation, Amazon FireTV and Alexa, and a 4G LTE Wi-Fi hotspot.

The Recon comes standard with many safety and assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, a 360-degree surround camera, and parking assist.

#4523. BYD is launching this 5-seat luxury electric SUV next week with over 1,000 km of range

BYD’s luxury brand, Denza, calls it “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles.” The new Denza N8 electric SUV will launch next week, offering an impressive CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles), massive digital screens, and plenty of premium extras.

After opening pre-orders for the new 5-seat luxury electric SUV last week, Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, said the results so far “have been excellent.”

According to Li, the Denza N8 is “definitely the most anticipated luxury SUV of the year.” Using BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries, the Denza N8 EV has a pure electric CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) on a single charge.

That’s just as much as the N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

While Li confirmed last week that the new EV variant would go on sale in November, he didn’t give a specific date.

Now, it’s official. Denza announced on its Weibo page on Friday that the launch event for the Denza N8 EV will be held on November 12, 2026.

BYD is still offering a limited-time promo that includes a 5,000 RMB credit for those who place a reservation with a 2,000 RMB ($200) deposit.

The Denza N8 measures 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase. That’s slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

It’s available with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).

The tri-motor Denza N8 uses BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

Regulatory filings earlier this year revealed it will use either a 130.15 kWh or 105.79 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 1,003 km (623 miles) and 800 km (497 miles), respectively.

The Denza N8 also features BYD’s latest Flash Charging technology, letting it recharge from 10% to 80% in just five minutes. It takes just nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat electric SUV features a massive 30″ infotainment screen that spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, plus a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

Like most of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is loaded with BYD’s latest software and technology.

Added premium features include zero-gravity seating in all rows, a three-spoke steering wheel, wireless phone chargers, and ambient lighting.

The electric SUV is equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR to support BYD’s God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system, plus its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system.

BYD has yet to announce prices for the Denza N8 EV, but it will likely be slightly less than the N8L, an extended version that starts at 299,800 RMB ($45,000).

#4522. Polestar Formula 2030 Station Wagon Concept Offers a Futuristic Blueprint for Scandinavian Design

Polestar’s head of design, Philipp Römers, is laying out the visual language of tomorrow for the all-electric brand.

Before Polestar’s public battle with the U.S. Department of Commerce earlier this year, the Swedish automaker was perhaps best known here for its avant-garde Scandinavian design language. Now, it seems like Polestar is simply teasing us after being banned from the United States starting in 2027, as the newly revealed Polestar Formula 2030 concept car is one of the coolest wagons we’ve ever seen.

The Formula 2030 concept car is the creation of Polestar’s head of design, Philipp Römers, and opens a window into the company’s future direction. The brand’s “remove the unnecessary, improve what remains, and refuse to compromise” design philosophy led the project, and Römers said the model is a practical four-door sports car. At 184 inches long, 79.5 inches wide, and with a 109-inch wheelbase, the Polestar Formula 2030 is sized between the outgoing Polestar 2 sedan and the incoming Polestar 7 hatchback. Polestar declined to provide any mechanical details about the Formula 2030.

“Design should always reflect the values and mission of a brand, and that is exactly what we did with Polestar Formula 2030 concept,” Römers said. “It is a physical embodiment of how we apply Polestar‘s core values of design, performance, and sustainability to the next production cars. A bold evolution of our already well-established design DNA to strengthen the brand‘s positioning with performance at its heart.”

A long hood, short overhangs, and 22-inch center-lock wheels exemplify the classic Polestar look, while also expressing “power and performance.” Dual-blade headlights mark the front end and serve as a preview of the updated Polestar 2, which will arrive in 2027. The shark nose and deep front splitter create the central spine of the Formula 2030 and give it a low and wide stance, adding to its performance credentials. A single large windscreen wiper pays homage to motorsport.

Polestar’s Single Blade rear lights highlight the rear end; instead of a connected light bar, the company wanted to explore new geometric shapes and angles. The rear glass also wraps around the side of the vehicle, opening a shallow side-view behind the C-pillar. A fixed rear wing sits on lit mounts, while the lower rear diffuser adds genuine downforce.

“We wanted to evolve, while respecting, the core design values we demonstrated with previous models that define the Polestar brand in such a recognizable way. And with Formula 2030, with its clear Polestar design attributes like the Dual Blade headlights, wraparound visor-like windshield and powerful haunches, we have done just that,” Nahum Escobedo, head of exterior design at Polestar, said. “But we’ve pushed perceptions, preconceptions, and the expected as well, with our considered choices in form language, amplification of the performance topic, and new detailing like the Single Blade rear lights.”

Inside the Formula 2030, the automaker stuck with minimalism. A 12.2-inch Center Screen Display is paired with the 20-inch “HyperDIM”—a precisely curved Driver Information Monitor—to round out the digital offerings. Air-inflatable bolsters are fitted to each seat to balance cushioned comfort and performance-oriented ergonomics. When combined with Polestar’s three drive modes—Performance, Normal, and Autonomous—the center displays and adjustable seats will position themselves for the mood; for example, in Performance mode, the steering wheel, screens, and seats will lower and move toward the driver. Similarly, Polestar will offer a configurable mix of physical and digital controls in the center stack; users can choose which controls they want to be actioned by the physical buttons. (Attentive readers will also notice a steering yoke in place of the typical steering wheel.)

Finally, the Polestar Formula 2030 shows off a new “Nitrogen” exterior color, which is specific to the concept. Variations of the new color in gloss, matte, and satin finishes are scattered around the car. Polestar’s characteristic Swedish Gold color adorns the Brembo brake calipers, valve caps, interior detailing, and seat belts. The interior finish of the doors is made from a fully recyclable material, which is contrasted by exposed structural interior parts such as the seat frame made from low-emission galvanized steel. All told, the Polestar Formula 2030 offers a compelling glimpse of what’s ahead for the Swedish automaker, and we’re sure sad to miss out on it.

#4520. China's World-Beating Supercar Just Hit 312 MPH

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A Chinese EV is officially the fastest production car in the world and the first production car in history to break the 500 kilometers per hour (310 miles per hour) barrier. BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme, a two-door electric hypercar, reached 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) on a public road in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on November 1.

As a reminder, the U9 Xtreme was already the world’s fastest car, after it reached 496.22 kph (308.3 mph) back in September 2025, but the Chinese automaker had already set its sights last year on breaking the 500 kph barrier—something that no other production car has ever managed.

The latest and most impressive record happened on a roughly 10-kilometer (6.2-mile) stretch of the E11 road in Abu Dhabi’s Al Dhafra Region, which was closed to public traffic. German racing driver Marc Basseng, the same driver who delivered the previous record, was behind the wheel and needed four runs over the course of two days to set the new record.

The first two runs happened on October 31, when the maximum speed was 490 kph (304.4 mph). Engineers made adjustments to the vehicle’s aerodynamics, suspension settings, and tire pressures to improve stability and performance. Then, on the last run of the second day, the Racelogic recorder made the 503.17 kph (312.6 mph) run official.

According to Guinness World Records, the Yangwang U9 Xtreme now holds the records for the highest speed achieved by a production car and an electric production car in a single-direction run. The FIA also confirmed the achievement on its website.

That last part is particularly interesting because the usual way of breaking records involves two separate runs in opposite directions to account for elevation change, wind speed, and any potential breakdown. BYD went for a single run in a single direction, which could make companies like Rimac, Bugatti, and Koenigsegg raise an eyebrow and challenge BYD’s result.

Nevertheless, going over 500 kph in a production car—albeit a limited-production model—is immensely impressive, especially considering that it’s an EV. BYD plans to make just 30 units of the U9 Xtreme, which is the most powerful and fastest version of the U9 supercar. Powered by four electric motors totaling 2,977 horsepower, the Xtreme uses a 1,200-volt lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack that can discharge at a 30C rate. A set of semi-slick GitiSport e-GTR2 Pro tires keeps the car on the road and provides stopping power, helped by titanium calipers and carbon-ceramic rotors.

#4519. EVgo opens its first Tesla Superchargers, with hundreds more planned

EVgo has opened its first Supercharger station, and it’s in a Chicago grocery store parking lot. The site has 12 fast-charging stalls with both NACS and CCS plugs, and it’s the first of hundreds of Tesla Supercharger stalls EVgo plans to add across the US.

The 325 kW “EVgo Superchargers” are at Riverside Square & River’s Edge, at 3145 S Ashland Avenue. EVgo’s August announcement cited up to 500 kW for the Supercharger rollout.

The Chicago location features Magic Dock technology, which means both NACS and CCS vehicles can charge without an adapter. Drivers of compatible non-Tesla EVs can start a session through the Tesla app. If you drive a Tesla, the charging station shows up in the car’s navigation and Trip Planner. Other EVgo fast chargers with NACS plugs have been showing up in Tesla navigation since early September if you turn on third-party charging.

“By serving both Tesla and non-Tesla NACS drivers, we’re doubling EVgo’s addressable market and continuing to meet EV drivers where they are and where they want to charge,” said Badar Khan, EVgo CEO.

EVgo owns the Superchargers and self-brands them, and Tesla runs and maintains them. The first sites will be at Regency Centers shopping plazas with grocery stores.

Smart move on EVGo's part. More reliable charger at a lower cost than they can build themselves, and Tesla takes on all the maintenance and network operations for a slice of the sales.

EVgo is also adding NACS plugs to its regular fast-charging network, a rollout it started in 2025. The company aims to have 500 of those stalls across the US by the end of 2026, with Supercharger stalls counted separately. Over the next two years, it plans to put at least one NACS plug at every EVgo site built in 2023 or later.

#4518. 2027 Ford Mustang GTD

Typically, when "$300,000" and "pony" appear in the same sentence, what's likely the subject of discussion is purebred racehorses. The talk, however, could now also be about the Ford Mustang GTD. If its name, ultrawide bodywork, carbon-fiber diffusers, and shade-casting rear wing weren’t dead giveaways, know that the GTD is as close as you can get to an IMSA race car for the road. In fact, with 815 horsepower supplied by a supercharged 5.2-liter V-8, it has far more power than the Mustang GT3 race cars that competed in this year's 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Power is only one aspect of the GTD's expansive performance envelope, and with a carbon fiber body, sophisticated underbody active aerodynamics, and a race-car-derived inboard pushrod suspension setup where a standard 'Stang's rear seats would be, it's no wonder why Ford's ultimate pony is the second fastest production car around the Nürburgring Nordschleife. As is usually the case, performance comes at a cost. In the GTD's case, that is both literal and figurative, with its supercar-rivaling MSRP and a dearth of space for either passengers or cargo.

Expert Tip: With 1250 horsepower, a 0-60-mph sprint time of 2.1 seconds, and a starting price $100,000 less than the GTD, the Corvette ZR1X arguably offers a superior performance-to-price ratio than Ford's ultimate Mustang.

With 815 horsepower from its supercharged 5.2-liter V-8 engine, the road-going car has far more power than the Mustang GT3 race car it shares styling with. That track-only model instead uses a 5.4-liter V-8 with around 550 horsepower. Cog swaps for the GTD come courtesy of a rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch automated transaxle, similar to the type of gearbox used in the race car.

A Mustang GTD we tested blew us away with its performance. Its shockingly civilized on-road ride quality surprised us as well. We would welcome more steering feedback, but the supremely balanced handling and staggering levels of grip make for a world-class driving experience.
